correctness.rationale: The Ferreira–Speziali diagonal classification is a stated hypothesis from a primary 2022 paper, supported by its Theorem 4.4 and q=5 Proposition 4.1. Every rational point of its model is toric; Gauss differentiation gives a bijection to the rational dual torus; the elementary nonzero-linear-equation count proves all three multiplicity strata with exact projective quantifiers for every q>=5. The q=5 square-coefficient comparison handles all three support types of lines, constructs 28 geometrically distinct even-contact lines, and identifies Frobenius roots in degree-4 Kummer extension; Frobenius cycle counts are independently confirmed by exact GF(625) code. No finite calculation is claimed to imply the all-q statement.

originality.rationale: The new object is the rational Gauss-dual incidence profile of every already-classified Sziklai-optimal degree-(q-1) curve and the finite-field Frobenius odd-theta profile of the q=5 member. Existing classification determines the equation and count of rational curve points, not this transverse dual-incidence theorem; tangent-filling literature treats a different property and supplies q-1 examples not Sziklai-extremal. Complex Fermat group actions and classical 28-line formulas are explicitly treated as potentially covering the geometric bitangent list, but they do not state the combined all-q tangent-deficit theorem or its F5 arithmetic refinement. Actual research-record, arXiv HTML, and text-search comparisons yielded no equivalent statement. Priority remains fallible, especially for historical classical geometry.

value.rationale: The Sziklai bound and tangent-filling property are independently prominent, mathematically motivated finite-field plane-curve notions. The exact infinite-family three-point obstruction and full incidence profile settle their interaction at the highest possible point count for degree q-1, explaining why the degree-(q-1) tangent-filling examples of Asgarli–Ghioca must lie outside the sharp Sziklai locus. At q=5 the natural odd-theta/bitangent arithmetic Frobenius profile is completely explicit, providing information independent of the rational point count. This is not a mere code or small-field normalization: the main theorem is uniform in every prime-power q>=5, while the quartic clause records a natural exact arithmetic invariant. No larger consequence or novelty of the classical Fermat-bitangent list is claimed.
